questions.question: According to the article, what is the cell?
options: The structural and functional unit of life
A type of macromolecule found only in eukaryotes
The basic unit of reproduction in all living things
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'The cell is the structural and functional unit of life.'
Incorrect. The article does not describe the cell as the smallest known living organism.
Incorrect. The article describes proteins and nucleic acids as macromolecules, not the cell.
Incorrect. While cells are involved in reproduction, the article specifically defines the cell as the structural and functional unit of life, not the basic unit of reproduction.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a descriptive trait of life in the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. Homeostasis is listed as the first descriptive trait of life: 'regulation of the internal environment to maintain a constant state.'
Incorrect. Photosynthesis is not listed among the descriptive traits of life in the article.
Incorrect. Cellular respiration is not listed among the descriptive traits of life in the article.
Incorrect. Genetic mutation is not listed among the descriptive traits of life in the article.

questions.question: According to the article, what is a biota?
options: The life in a particular ecosystem
A type of extremophile found in harsh environments
The process by which cells signal to one another
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'The life in a particular ecosystem is called its biota.'
Incorrect. Extremophiles are organisms that occupy harsh environments, but they are not called biota.
Incorrect. Cell signalling is a biological process, not a biota.
Incorrect. Binomial nomenclature is Carl Linnaeus's classification system, not a biota.

questions.question: According to the article, why are viruses controversial in discussions of life?
options: They replicate only in host cells and do not metabolise
They are composed of four eternal elements
They cannot evolve by natural selection
They are always classified as forms of life
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that viruses 'replicate only in host cells' and 'do not metabolise,' which complicates whether they should be considered alive.
Incorrect. The four eternal elements are part of Empedocles's materialist theory, not a property of viruses.
Incorrect. The article states that viruses 'evolve by natural selection,' so this is not a reason for controversy.
Incorrect. The article states viruses are 'most often considered as just gene-coding replicators rather than forms of life,' so they are not always classified as alive.

questions.question: According to Aristotle's hylomorphism, what is the form of a living thing?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'the form of a living thing is its soul (Greek psyche, Latin anima).'
Incorrect. Matter and form are distinct concepts in hylomorphism; the form is not the matter itself.
Incorrect. The four eternal elements are part of Empedocles's materialism, not Aristotle's hylomorphism.
Incorrect. Biochemical molecules are discussed in a later section on the composition of living things, not in Aristotle's hylomorphism.

questions.question: According to the article, what did Louis Pasteur's experiments in 1859 decisively dispel?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that spontaneous generation 'was decisively dispelled by the experiments of Louis Pasteur in 1859.'
Incorrect. Hylomorphism is Aristotle's theory and is not said to have been dispelled by Pasteur.
Incorrect. Materialism is a broader philosophical theory and is not said to have been dispelled by Pasteur.
Incorrect. Natural selection is Charles Darwin's theory and is not said to have been dispelled by Pasteur.

questions.question: According to the article, what two types of macromolecules do all living things contain?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'All living things contain two types of macromolecules, proteins and nucleic acids.'
Incorrect. Carbohydrates and lipids are not mentioned as the two macromolecules all living things contain.
Incorrect. The article says nucleic acids are usually both DNA and RNA, not that DNA and proteins are the only two types.
Incorrect. RNA is a nucleic acid, but lipids are not one of the two macromolecule types mentioned.

questions.question: According to the article, what criticism is made of the NASA definition of life as 'a self-sustained chemical system capable of undergoing Darwinian evolution'?
options: A single sexually reproducing individual is not alive as it is incapable of evolving on its own
It does not account for viruses
It requires life to be composed of cells
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states this definition 'has been widely criticised because, according to it, a single sexually reproducing individual is not alive as it is incapable of evolving on its own.'
Incorrect. The article does not mention viruses in connection with the criticism of the NASA definition.
Incorrect. The article does not state that the definition requires life to be composed of cells.
Incorrect. The article does not state that the definition excludes extraterrestrial life.

questions.question: According to the article, what is metabolism?
options: Transformation of energy used to convert chemicals into cellular components and to decompose organic matter
Regulation of the internal environment to maintain a constant state
The evolutionary process whereby an organism becomes better able to live in its habitat
The ability to produce new individual organisms
answer_explanations: Correct. The article defines metabolism as 'transformation of energy, used to convert chemicals into cellular components (anabolism) and to decompose organic matter (catabolism).'
Incorrect. Regulation of the internal environment is homeostasis, not metabolism.
Incorrect. The evolutionary process whereby an organism becomes better able to live in its habitat is adaptation, not metabolism.
Incorrect. The ability to produce new individual organisms is reproduction, not metabolism.

questions.question: According to the article, where is life known to exist?
options: On Earth and on other planets
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states: 'Life is only known to exist on Earth.'
Incorrect. The article says life is only known to exist on Earth, though extraterrestrial life is thought to be probable.
Incorrect. The article says life exists in air, water, and soil, not only in air and water.
Incorrect. The article says life exists in air, water, and soil, not only in soil.
